title: Eridu found in the 1800s, its ziggurat never excavated
summary: Matt tells of Eridu found in the 1800s, its ziggurat never excavated, about late 1800s; World War II at Eridu, southern Iraq, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: so in the 1800s they find aido and they only excavate the main part of the city they find tablets and everything they bring them to the British museum they never excavate the arido zigon

plain: A researcher named Matt, speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that in the 1800s explorers found Eridu, an ancient city in southern Iraq, dug up only its main part, and sent the clay tablets they found to the British Museum. According to Matt, they never excavated Eridu's ziggurat, a large stepped temple tower, which he suggests could still hold answers about the deep past.
